note: Cameras permanently excluded from the shipped fixture, applied by scripts/export-mobile-assets.mjs. A camera listed here is dropped from mobile/src/data/bands.json and can never be re-added by an export -- not by --source fixture, not by --only, not from state.json or learned-bands.json. Removing a row is the only way back, and it should be done only with a fresh overlay proving the camera holds the view its geometry was learned on. The band-loss guard deliberately ignores these ids: disabling one is an intended loss, not the accident the guard exists to catch. Of 208 City cameras the app covers a hand-picked few, so a camera that cannot be trusted is cheap to drop and expensive to keep.

fields.why: one line: what makes this camera unusable

162.why: PTZ: the camera no longer holds the view its band was learned on.
162.evidence: Corner direction label read E on the learning-era frame (data/debug-162.jpg) and W live. The shipped band drawn on a current frame crosses the roadway and the crosswalk instead of lying on a curb. Re-learning from data/history/162.jsonl (303 rows) yields ZERO bands, which is what a view change looks like to the learner.

182.why: PTZ: the camera no longer holds the view its band was learned on, and the band was never sound to begin with.
182.evidence: Corner direction label read SW on the learning-era frame (data/debug-182.jpg) and NW live; 12 frames sampled over 4 minutes all held the new view. The shipped band drawn on a current frame runs diagonally across both travel lanes. Independently, the band fails today's learner: sideFrac 0.74 in state.json against minSideFrac 0.8 ('traffic both sides'), only 13.9 m of its claimed 33.3 m ever observed (coreT 145.2-440.8 of 697.1 px), and 33.3 m claimed against a 23.9 m zone.

169.why: The band lies on the Holt Renfrew sidewalk, not on a curb. No part of the corridor has roadway under it.
169.evidence: Drawn on a live frame (npm run diag:overlay), the whole corridor runs along the shopfront at 8 Av / 1 St SW with pedestrians walking through it; the real parked-car row is off to the right, past the traffic signal, and the band never reaches it. The view is stable, not mid-pan: four frames over two minutes differ by 2.7-4.3/255 mean greyscale. There is no learning-era frame for this camera, so whether the camera panned or the fit was always wrong cannot be settled -- it does not need to be, because the shipped geometry is wrong against today's view either way. Independently: 137 support over a 7.0 m core split into 3 slots is 2.3 m per slot, physically impossible for parallel parking, and no history is collected for it so `freeT` cannot bound what it may claim.

171.why: The band runs off the curb, down the travel lane and out through the intersection. It reported 8.5 m free -- and PARK -- in a live traffic lane.
171.evidence: Two independent frames agree: on the archived daytime snapshot (data/snapshots/171-1787427682000.jpg) the corridor crosses the crosswalk and leaves the frame at the bottom-right corner, and on a live frame its 'occupied' run covers cars stopped at the red light rather than parked at a kerb. The view is stable over two minutes (mean greyscale delta 4.3-5.9/255), so this is not a pan caught in progress. It carries the weakest evidence of any shipped band -- support 67, against 89 for the next lowest and 481 for camera 27 -- and it cannot be reproduced from anything in this repo: state.json's own 171 band is a different line entirely (226 px, core 94-185) from the shipped one (507 px, core 65-301), which came from a research-repo export. No history is collected for it, so `freeT` cannot bound what it claims.
